findings.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:57 — `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&` between `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)`, so only a team owner satisfies it and team admins are incorrectly denied; should almost certainly be `||`

[High/bug] addGuests.handler.ts:160-165 — `EventManager` is built with `ctx.user` (the caller) and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, but the calendar event belongs to the booking's organizer (`booking.user`); `updateCalendarAttendees` runs with wrong credentials and fails to find/update the event; should use the booking organizer's user/credentials as `editLocation.handler` does

[Medium/security] addGuests.handler.ts:69-72 — `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` are lowercased but the incoming `guest` email is not, so `Spam@X.com` bypasses a blacklist entry for `spam@x.com`; normalize guest emails with `.toLowerCase()` before filtering

[Medium/data] addGuests.handler.ts:75-80 — Duplicate detection against existing attendees is case-sensitive (`guest === attendee.email`) and the input array is never deduped server-side (uniqueness only enforced client-side), so `"a@x.com"` and `"A@x.com"` or repeated emails create duplicate attendees and send duplicate emails; dedupe/lowercase in the schema or handler

[Medium/security] addGuests.handler.ts:47-67 — Any booking attendee (not just the organizer) is authorized to add an unlimited number of guests and the schema has no max bound on `guests`, allowing any attendee to trigger mass invitation emails (email-bombing/spam vector); restrict to organizer/admin and cap array length (e.g. `z.array(...).max(N)`)

[Medium/bug] addGuests.handler.ts:33-40 — Booking lookup doesn't exclude cancelled/rejected bookings, so guests can be added (and "CONFIRMED" ics REQUEST emails sent) for a cancelled event; add a status check (`NOT` in cancelled statuses)

[Medium/concurrency] addGuests.handler.ts:86-97 — Attendee read, permission checks, and `prisma.booking.update` (createMany) are not wrapped in a transaction or guarded against concurrent submissions, so two simultaneous `addGuests` calls can both pass the duplicate check and insert the same guests twice; use a transaction and/or unique constraint, and consider upsert-style dedupe inside createMany data

[Medium/data] addGuests.handler.ts:172-175 — Email-sending errors are swallowed with `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging the error object, and the handler still returns success after the DB write; at minimum log `err` (structured logger) so failures are diagnosable

[Low/bug] apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:53-59 — `isInvalidEmail` is set on failed validation but never cleared on input change or successful submit, so the "Emails must be unique and valid" warning persists after the user fixes the emails and reappears when the dialog is reopened via backdrop/Escape close

[Low/bug] addGuests.handler.ts:85-92 — `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` throws an unhandled `NotFoundError` (500 instead of a proper TRPC error) when the booking has no `userId`, and the `|| 0` sentinel is fragile; validate and throw `NOT_FOUND`/`BAD_REQUEST` explicitly
[Low/bug] packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:47 — Tooltip content `"Remove email"` is a hardcoded English string, not passed through `t()` unlike all other UI text, so it will not be translated

[Low/bug] packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:27 — List items use `key={index}` while rows can be spliced out; after a removal, React reuses inputs by index which can leave stale DOM state/uncontrolled input values; use a stable id per email entry

[Low/api] apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:41-44 — Error toast builds `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`; for non-translation-key messages `t()` echoes the raw key, and the `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is unreachable since the template string is always truthy; prefer showing a translated message only when one exists

[Low/test_gap] No tests added for `addGuestsHandler` (authorization matrix: organizer/admin/owner/attendee/unrelated user, duplicate/blacklist filtering, cancelled bookings) or for `sendAddGuestsEmails` routing (new guests vs existing attendees), despite security-sensitive logic

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] addGuests.handler.ts:160-165 — `EventManager` is built with `ctx.user` (the caller) and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, but the calendar event belongs to the booking's organizer (`booking.user`); `updateCalendarAttendees` runs with wrong credentials and fails to find/update the event; should use the booking organizer's user/credentials as `editLocation.handler` does

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation explicitly permits non-organizers to add guests (team admin/owner, organizer, or any attendee). However, the calendar update is performed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] }); await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` where `user` is the caller (`ctx.user`), not the booking organizer. The booking organizer is fetched separately (`organizer`) and `booking.user` is included with `credentials`, but neither is used to build the `EventManager`. If the caller is an attendee/team member, this will attempt to update the organizer’s event using the wrong account/credentials and is likely to fail or update the wrong calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] addGuests.handler.ts:47-67 — Any booking attendee (not just the organizer) is authorized to add an unlimited number of guests and the schema has no max bound on `guests`, allowing any attendee to trigger mass invitation emails (email-bombing/spam vector); restrict to organizer/admin and cap array length (e.g. `z.array(...).max(N)`)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, authorization explicitly allows any existing attendee to add guests: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and the request is permitted when `isAttendee` is true (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw ...`). Additionally, the input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(N)` bound, so an attendee can submit an arbitrarily large list and trigger `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` to send many emails. This matches the reported spam/email-bombing vector and is directly evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] addGuests.handler.ts:33-40 — Booking lookup doesn't exclude cancelled/rejected bookings, so guests can be added (and "CONFIRMED" ics REQUEST emails sent) for a cancelled event; add a status check (`NOT` in cancelled statuses)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking is fetched with `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })` and there is no check/filter on any booking status before updating attendees (`prisma.booking.update(...)`) and sending calendar/ICS updates using `status: "CONFIRMED"` in the email templates. If cancelled/rejected bookings exist in the system, this mutation would still allow adding guests and emit CONFIRMED updates for a non-active booking, which is incorrect behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] addGuests.handler.ts:86-97 — Attendee read, permission checks, and `prisma.booking.update` (createMany) are not wrapped in a transaction or guarded against concurrent submissions, so two simultaneous `addGuests` calls can both pass the duplicate check and insert the same guests twice; use a transaction and/or unique constraint, and consider upsert-style dedupe inside createMany data

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, deduping is done in application code using the initially fetched `booking.attendees` (`uniqueGuests = guests.filter(!booking.attendees.some(...))`), then a separate `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` inserts rows. There’s no transaction and no DB-level/`createMany({ skipDuplicates: true })` protection shown, so two concurrent `addGuests` requests can both see the same pre-update attendee list and both insert the same guest emails, causing duplicate attendees.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] addGuests.handler.ts:172-175 — Email-sending errors are swallowed with `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging the error object, and the handler still returns success after the DB write; at minimum log `err` (structured logger) so failures are diagnosable

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and discards the caught `err`, then the handler still returns success after the DB update. This is diff-grounded (the `catch (err) { console.log(...) }` block) and is a diagnosability/observability concern rather than a clearly verifiable functional defect, since continuing after email failure may be intentional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:53-59 — `isInvalidEmail` is set on failed validation but never cleared on input change or successful submit, so the "Emails must be unique and valid" warning persists after the user fixes the emails and reappears when the dialog is reopened via backdrop/Escape close

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on failed validation (`handleAdd` else branch) but is only cleared in the Cancel button handler. It is not cleared on input change (`MultiEmail` only updates `multiEmailValue`) nor on successful submission (`onSuccess` resets `multiEmailValue` and closes the dialog but does not call `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`). Since the dialog component remains mounted in `BookingListItem` and `onOpenChange` can close it via backdrop/Escape without resetting state, the warning can persist and reappear on reopen.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] addGuests.handler.ts:85-92 — `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` throws an unhandled `NotFoundError` (500 instead of a proper TRPC error) when the booking has no `userId`, and the `|| 0` sentinel is fragile; validate and throw `NOT_FOUND`/`BAD_REQUEST` explicitly

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer lookup uses `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. The `|| 0` sentinel implies `booking.userId` may be null/undefined; in that case Prisma will `throw` (record not found) and there is no surrounding `try/catch` or explicit `TRPCError` mapping for this path, so the mutation can surface as an unhandled/internal error rather than a deliberate `NOT_FOUND`/`BAD_REQUEST`. This is a fragile correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:47 — Tooltip content `"Remove email"` is a hardcoded English string, not passed through `t()` unlike all other UI text, so it will not be translated

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the remove icon tooltip uses a hardcoded string: `<Tooltip content="Remove email">` rather than a translated key via `t()`, while other UI strings in the component use `t(...)`. This creates an i18n/localization gap but doesn’t break functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:27 — List items use `key={index}` while rows can be spliced out; after a removal, React reuses inputs by index which can leave stale DOM state/uncontrolled input values; use a stable id per email entry

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the list of email inputs is rendered with `value.map((field, index) => <li key={index}> ...)` and items can be removed via `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`. Using the array index as the React key in a list where elements are deleted/inserted can cause React to reuse component instances for different rows, which can preserve per-row component/DOM state (e.g., focus, validation state inside `EmailField`) across removals. The diff shows this dynamic splice behavior, but because the input is controlled (`value={field}`), the “stale/uncontrolled input values” part isn’t strictly provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:41-44 — Error toast builds `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`; for non-translation-key messages `t()` echoes the raw key, and the `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is unreachable since the template string is always truthy; prefer showing a translated message only when one exists

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx onError, `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` will always produce a truthy string (even if `err.data?.code` is undefined), so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), ...)` makes the fallback effectively unreachable. Also `t(err.message)` assumes `err.message` is a translation key; the diff shows server errors use keys like `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, but other TRPC errors could produce non-key messages, leading to confusing output rather than a clean translated fallback. This is a UX/robustness issue rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] No tests added for `addGuestsHandler` (authorization matrix: organizer/admin/owner/attendee/unrelated user, duplicate/blacklist filtering, cancelled bookings) or for `sendAddGuestsEmails` routing (new guests vs existing attendees), despite security-sensitive logic

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new security/permission-sensitive behavior and nontrivial branching without any accompanying tests in the shown changes: `addGuestsHandler` adds authorization checks (`isTeamAdmin`/`isTeamOwner`, organizer, attendee) and filtering logic (existing attendees + `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`, `uniqueGuests.length === 0` error), plus side effects (DB update, calendar attendee update, and `sendAddGuestsEmails`). `sendAddGuestsEmails` also has routing logic that changes email template depending on whether an attendee is in `newGuests` (`newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`), which is easy to regress. While the finding mentions "cancelled bookings" (not present in the diff), the core point—no tests added for this new handler/email branching—is directly grounded in the diff.
